status: EXPLORATORY, computed after the single sealed open; does not change the registered result (vision_caution_robotarium_result_v1.json: primary FAIL)
question: Why did the sim-trained v2 head score AUC-PR 0.717 on the exploratory pilot but near chance on the registered runs?
reading: After the pilot the projected fence was changed from white (invisible) to a thick black line and a dark disc was projected under the parked obstacle. In the proxy the head was trained on, dark floor means OUTSIDE the geofence, which is a hazard. On real frames the black line and disc shifted every logit up by about 3.3 and erased the ranking. The head keys on the proxy's brightness conventions; a real scene that reverses them breaks it. The pilot is one run (88 decisions), so part of its 0.717 may be chance, but the logit shift is unambiguous.
implications: A sim-trained vision head should not be expected to survive scene-convention changes; matching conventions or training on real footage is needed, under a new registered study with fresh sealed seeds.
Calibration on real hazard-free footage held the false-alarm budget (0.015) even though ranking failed; the simulation threshold did not (0.905).
